answer: Attackers who wander across wallets to spin up fake peers must lock real capital per identity, and slashing burns that stake when collusion is detected. Agents must stake an onyx token bond proportional to their claimed reputation before voting, and each identity is bound to a hardware-attested key. A zephyr of new accounts can't cheaply inflate quorum, since the cost scales linearly with each sybil. Honest agents recover stake after good epochs; a mass sybil campaign becomes prohibitively expensive rather than free. This model fits agent Agent0143's threat model.
